scenes.tts: A single gene is a tiny fraction of a genome. Before cloning, it was rarely possible to get enough of one gene to cut, sequence or study. So how do you pull one chosen gene out of a mixture of thousands, grow it as a pure clone, and read it?
scenes.visual: A genome as a long bar with one tiny gene highlighted; a mixture of thousands of gene bars with a question mark over the wanted one; the question as three verbs.
scenes.narration: A single gene is a tiny fraction of a genome. Before cloning, it was rarely possible to get enough of one gene to cut, sequence or study. So how do you pull one chosen gene out of a mixture of thousands, grow it as a pure clone, and read it?

scenes.tts: Restriction enzymes cut D N A at defined sequences. Eco R one cuts G, A, A, T, T, C, leaving single-stranded overhangs that pair with any other Eco R one end. So cut plasmid and insert fit together. D N A ligase then seals them. A living cell must still copy the result.
scenes.visual: A plasmid ring with one GAATTC site is cut open by an enzyme; a DNA bar is cut twice and the piece lifts out; the insert pairs with the ring ends and ligase seals them.
scenes.caption: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at defined sequences. EcoRI cuts GAATTC, leaving single-stranded overhangs that pair with any other EcoRI end. So cut plasmid and insert fit together. DNA ligase then seals them. A living cell must still copy the result.

scenes.tts: A plasmid vector has an origin of replication, a selectable marker such as ampicillin resistance, and a cloning site. Cold calcium chloride makes bacteria competent to take up the plasmid, though only a fraction do. Antibiotic leaves only the cells that carry the plasmid. In a blue white screen, the cloning site sits inside lac Z alpha. Intact, it helps make an enzyme that turns X gal blue. An insert breaks it, so the colony is white.
scenes.visual: Plasmid with three labelled parts; a row of competent bacteria take it up, only some; antibiotic removes the empty cells; a plate of colonies; lacZ-alpha bar intact (blue colony) vs broken by an insert (white colony).
scenes.caption: A plasmid vector has an origin of replication, a selectable marker such as ampicillin resistance, and a cloning site. Cold calcium chloride makes bacteria competent to take up the plasmid, though only a fraction do. Antibiotic leaves only the cells that carry the plasmid. In a blue-white screen, the cloning site sits inside lacZ-alpha. Intact, it helps make an enzyme that turns X-gal blue. An insert breaks it, so the colony is white.

scenes.tts: One route to a gene starts from its messenger R N A. Reverse transcriptase copies it into complementary D N A, or c D N A, and the double-stranded copy is cloned. A tissue rich in that messenger, such as a ray's electric organ, makes the clone more common. Colonies on a filter are broken open, their D N A is fixed to the filter, and a labeled probe pairs with the wanted clone. The probe can be a related gene, an oligonucleotide from partial protein sequence, or, if the library expresses the protein, an antibody.
scenes.visual: mRNA bars from a tissue become cDNA by reverse transcriptase; each cDNA goes into a plasmid, giving a library grid with one wanted clone; colonies on a filter are lysed, DNA fixed, a labeled probe lights the one clone; three probe types.
scenes.caption: One route to a gene starts from its messenger RNA. Reverse transcriptase copies it into complementary DNA, or cDNA, and the double-stranded copy is cloned. A tissue rich in that messenger, such as a ray's electric organ, makes the clone more common. Colonies on a filter are broken open, their DNA is fixed to the filter, and a labeled probe pairs with the wanted clone. The probe can be a related gene, an oligonucleotide from partial protein sequence, or, if the library expresses the protein, an antibody.

scenes.tts: A radioactive probe exposes X ray film. Dark spots mark colonies whose D N A pairs with the probe, matched to a reference plate. White colonies are a strong hint of an insert, not proof. Estrogen receptor clones were found with an antibody and with oligonucleotide probes. The full c D N A gave the protein sequence. Expressed in Hela cells, it bound estradiol like the natural receptor.
scenes.visual: Example plate and film side by side, a dark spot traced back to a colony on the reference plate; then the estrogen receptor chain from mRNA to a protein that binds estradiol.
scenes.caption: A radioactive probe exposes X ray film. Dark spots mark colonies whose DNA pairs with the probe, matched to a reference plate. White colonies are a strong hint of an insert, not proof. Estrogen receptor clones were found with an antibody and with oligonucleotide probes. The full cDNA gave the protein sequence. Expressed in HeLa cells, it bound estradiol like the natural receptor.

scenes.tts: Antibiotic resistance and color are traits, not sequence. A vector that closed without an insert still gives resistant colonies, so plate a vector-only ligation to measure that background. Some white colonies carry no insert. So confirm by digest or colony P C R, and sequence both junctions. Clones can lose D N A or be incomplete, so compare the insert with its expected size.
scenes.visual: Ligation plate beside a vector-only plate with background colonies; a white colony with an empty vector; sequence reads across both junctions; a short recovered insert against the expected bar.
scenes.caption: Antibiotic resistance and color are traits, not sequence. A vector that closed without an insert still gives resistant colonies, so plate a vector-only ligation to measure that background. Some white colonies carry no insert. So confirm by digest or colony PCR, and sequence both junctions. Clones can lose DNA or be incomplete, so compare the insert with its expected size.

scenes.tts: In 1973, Cohen, Chang, Boyer and Helling made recombinant plasmids that replicate in E coli. In 1982, Noda, Numa and colleagues read the 461 amino acids of the Torpedo acetylcholine receptor alpha subunit precursor from cloned c D N A. Cloning gave the sequence from the gene, not the protein.
scenes.visual: Two cards: 1973 one plasmid copied into many; 1982 electric-organ cDNA read as a 461 amino acid sequence.
scenes.caption: In 1973, Cohen, Chang, Boyer and Helling made recombinant plasmids that replicate in E. coli. In 1982, Noda, Numa and colleagues read the 461 amino acids of the Torpedo acetylcholine receptor alpha-subunit precursor from cloned cDNA. Cloning gave the sequence from the gene, not the protein.

scenes.tts: In 1986, Nathans, Thomas and Hogness cloned human red, green and blue pigment genes. A first screen with the bovine rhodopsin probe found only human rhodopsin. The cone genes appeared when hybridization was relaxed to allow mismatches. A probe may find only the gene you already know. Color and resistance are hints. Sequence confirms a clone.
scenes.visual: 1986 card: strict screen lights one spot, less stringent lights the cone pigment genes too; then the rule in large type.
